name: Infrax Renewable Limited
sector: Solar rooftop and ground EPC; solar trading; proposed manufacturing; nascent IPP
summary: Infrax Renewable is a fast-growing rooftop EPC and solar-trading business, not yet a proven integrated manufacturer or power-generation compounder. FY26 revenue reached ₹93.21 crore and PAT ₹10.20 crore, but CFO was −₹2.70 crore as receivables and inventory absorbed cash. Manufacturing remains proposed; the small IPP had no FY26 revenue. At the dated secondary ₹169.25 close, current-share P/E is 23.62×. IPO capital strengthens the funding position, but complete current utilization, project cost and attributable return evidence is still missing. BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS are NS; classification is Hold — unresolved, not an automatic buy at a renewable-sector premium. Verified collections, funding and commissioning economics would change the assessment more than announcements.

Commodity trading, outsourced installation and no long-term customer/supplier contracts constrain pricing power.

EPC CAGR 142.36% and project-count CAGR 115.30% verify real demand expansion despite trading mix.

factor_audit.rationale: No trajectory adjustment or additional small-base penalty. Score uses comparable restated organic operating perimeter, not new factory capacity.

material_facts: Rooftop demand and distribution support several years of opportunity.
Gujarat concentration, subsidy-linked demand and supplier/customer contestability constrain duration.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Orderbook grew; plans can widen products if approvals and cash returns become real.

Mix shifts, idle/new IPP capital and planned manufacturing prevent attributing sustainable new-project returns.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Historical operating capital generated accounting profit; no inference that all new spending destroys value.
factor_audit.rationale: Current ROCE or a short changing-perimeter bridge does not establish attributable incremental returns; CAP is NS.

material_facts: Cumulative CFO/PAT −0.0562; FY26 receivables and inventory consume cash.
Tax liabilities remain material; source CFO includes financing-interest exclusion.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Most disclosed receivables are young and rapid expansion explains investment; no established pervasive bad-debt pattern.
factor_audit.rationale: Weak observed conversion, not proven permanent cash destruction. Score 4 avoids a mechanical persistent-CASH≤3 growth cap pending collection evidence.

Current unspent/restricted resources, complete machinery/civil/approval costs and on-demand repayment timing remain unverified.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Model base funds conservative annual obligations using disclosed proceeds under explicit assumptions.
factor_audit.rationale: Plausible financing is not established current financeability; no private daily bank statement is demanded. Published utilization and obligations bridge could suffice.

Manufacturing commissioning, quality yields and IPP receipts are not verified.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Company has executed a meaningful EPC ramp rather than only announcing orders.
factor_audit.rationale: Good past core execution but an untested manufacturing/asset-owning step change.

factor_audit.contrary_fact: Current-share EPS remains positive at ₹7.17, without applying pre-IPO weighted EPS to current shares.
factor_audit.rationale: Real operating profit, but repeatability and per-share durability are not yet high-confidence.

Linked slower collections, lower EPC margin and delayed factory sales threaten shareholder value.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Disclosed IPO capital and core EPC revenue provide a real buffer; actual default is not established.
factor_audit.rationale: Credible adverse recapitalization/permanent impairment path, not a certainty of distress.

material_facts: Current-share historical P/E is 23.62×; 15% hurdle needs 2.011× five-year wealth.
Reverse expectations require substantial profitable growth or multiple persistence without extra dilution.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: EPC has grown rapidly, and successful execution can support earnings growth.
factor_audit.rationale: Several favorable operating and capital assumptions must coexist; do not award a generic renewable premium.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exact issuer: Infrax Renewable Limited, CIN U43222GJ2024PLC155272, ISIN INE1YC401018, BSE SME 544919/INFRAX. Incorporation on 23 September 2024 followed the partnership Infrax International established in April 2019; the operating takeover was effective 1 November 2024. The official interoperable master includes this BSE security; it does not establish an NSE listing. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026, India time. Documents retrieved on 21 October are used only for pre-cutoff disclosures. The market reference is a cross-checked secondary 19 October close of ₹169.25, not a live executable offer. Market capitalization is ₹240.9428 crore using 14,235,911 shares.

Financial scope is standalone AS/Indian GAAP with predecessor-inclusive restated FY24–26; no consolidated subsidiary or NCI is evidenced. FY25 company-only statutory statements cover five months and are not substituted. FY22/23 and H1FY27 full comparable accounts are ND. Investor dates are 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, with a 15% nominal pre-tax equity hurdle and no assumed dividends. The ₹5 lakh position is illustrative, not personalized: two 1,200-share lots cost ₹406,200; three cost ₹609,300. Confidence is high for primary historical tables/identity, medium for organic economics and dated secondary price, low for future returns, current funding and liquidity. Gates G1/G2 are Conditional; G3/G4 are Hold — unresolved.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Factor points are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL NS, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R NS, D 3, P 4 and L NS. GQS means Growth Quality, not governance. IAS P means Price-implied expectations. Exact Decimal weights and contributions are retained below and in the canonical record. BQS coverage is 80%, known contribution 4.24 and missingness bounds 4.44–6.24. GQS coverage is 85%, known contribution 5.70 and bounds 5.85–7.20. IAS directly scored coverage is 30%, known contribution 1.00 and unpropagated bounds 1.70–8.00; propagating the BQS interval gives 2.56–7.06. None is a rankable score or a midpoint estimate.

The ≥30% growth starting REV score of 9 is capped at 8 for short history/medium confidence. There is no extra small-base penalty or unsupported trajectory uplift. CAP and BAL are missing for evidence reasons, not set to neutral 5. CASH 4 recognizes poor realized conversion with identifiable growth working capital, rather than asserting persistent value destruction. No automatic CAP/CASH≤3 override is triggered. A one-point change to a scored input changes only its exact weighted contribution; it does not repair missing factors or gates. All ordinary return and entry fields remain null, hence R and IAS are NS.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Four different businesses must be separated. FY26 residential rooftop EPC generated ₹46.6485 crore (50.04% of sales), ground EPC ₹7.8660 crore (8.44%), and trading solar products ₹38.7003 crore (41.52%). EPC earns project contribution after modules, balance-of-system material, contractors and execution; cash depends on advances, milestones and collections. Trading earns spread and turns inventory, not an IPP annuity. Installation and five years of free maintenance primarily through dealers/third parties are service obligations, not independently billed recurring revenue.

Manufacturing had zero historical revenue. Proposed recycling/silver extraction, mounting structures and aluminium frames have different feedstock, utilization, yield, customer-qualification and working-capital economics. No module-manufacturing profit is imputed. The Bhadla, Jasdan, Gujarat plant is described as 1.2 MW and operational since February 2026, with a 25-year PGVCL PPA, yet there was no FY26 IPP revenue. PPA duration does not establish tariff, CUF, receipts or equity return. A 1 MW commitment-note reference is preserved as an unresolved sizing detail, not silently treated as the same AC/DC measure.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is local dealer reach, project delivery and relationships, not a scarce renewable licence or proprietary manufacturing process. Dealers rose from 720 to 2,022 to 2,830 while FY26 rooftop jobs reached 3,078. Network expansion can lower acquisition friction, but dealers are not exclusive customers and third-party installation reduces both fixed costs and control. Four technical staff out of 52 employees leaves substantial dependence on counterparties. Gujarat supplied 97.41% of FY26 revenue. Top ten customers increased to 47.02% of sales; top ten suppliers supplied 65.86%. No long-term binding customer/supplier contracts were established.

Peer roles matter more than a renewable label. The issuer’s prospectus compares ACME Solar, Alpex Solar and Solarium Green Energy. ACME’s asset-owning IPP has contracted generation, high EBITDA margins, long asset life and leverage. Alpex module manufacturing depends on throughput, technology, procurement and policy. Solarium EPC is closer to project execution, but mix, scale, collections and contracts still differ. These issuer-reproduced peer data are not independently reconciled current comparable valuations. No sector premium or IPP multiple is applied to trading/EPC earnings. Failure modes are dealer churn, cheaper panels compressing revenue/spread, subsidy delays, warranty obligations and loss of execution quality during geographic expansion.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable restated revenue grew from ₹9.6524 crore in FY24 to ₹30.4686 crore in FY25 and ₹93.2149 crore in FY26: annual additions ₹20.8162 crore and ₹62.7463 crore. Two-year reported CAGR is 210.76%; three-/five-year CAGR is unavailable, not zero. The predecessor-to-company conversion is not a fresh acquisition of unrelated demand. Trading revenue grew faster than EPC and lifts gross reported scale; reported sales are not called pure unit growth.

EPC revenue rose ₹9.2811 → ₹23.6440 → ₹54.5145 crore, a 142.36% two-year CAGR. Rooftop count 664 → 1,964 → 3,078 gives 115.30%. FY26 rooftop revenue per project is about ₹1.52 lakh, against ₹1.20 lakh in FY25; this is average project scope/realization, not proof of unit price hikes for identical systems. No volume/price bridge is disclosed for trading. The August orderbook of 3,100 jobs/₹62.4419 crore is a dated snapshot, not already recognized revenue or guaranteed profit. The May orderbook and June recognition cannot be added without a cancellation/intake bridge. No verified H1FY27 results justify annualizing a quarter or upgrading the trend.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Core rooftop demand provides a credible accessible runway, but profitable scaling requires collections and inventory discipline. FY26 CFO fell below zero despite record PAT. Proposed factory capacity is 3,000 tonnes/year recycling, 1,500 tonnes/year mounting structures and 9.6 million frames/year. These physical outputs cannot be added together, priced at a generic panel realization, or valued as installed capacity. Machinery allocation ₹12.2933 crore excludes material civil, installation, transit, taxes and other costs; quoted foreign-currency equipment pricing creates execution and currency risk. Required operating approvals, customer qualification, production yield and utilization remain key hurdles.

Fresh IPO net cash ₹31.32572 crore plus June placement gross ₹7.0927992 crore are explicit funding sources. The OFS ₹7.07616 crore is not company cash. Machinery, working capital and general corporate objects reserve the IPO proceeds for intended uses. The annual model pays opening tax and employee obligations, cash-credit/promoter/current-term debt, civil costs, import taxes and maintenance without assuming deposit release or an undisclosed refinancing facility. A base modeled surplus is not proof of unspent cash or project financeability. Aggregate normalized incremental ROIC is 38.62%, but the changing mix and new plant perimeter make it a diagnostic, not a reliable attributable project return. CAP remains NS and GQS incomplete.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The historical EPC delivery record is a positive counterweight to promotional capacity language. The management team has scaled actual installations and a dealer network. Minority protections cannot be inferred from growth: September promoter ownership is 49.73%, public 50.27%, with no promoter pledge reported, but substantial shares remain locked. FY26 related trade with Infrax Solar LLP comprises sales ₹4.0143 crore, purchases ₹3.7390 crore and closing receivable ₹2.2881 crore. It is material to monitor, not proof of diversion. ₹0.25 crore related advances were repaid with interest during FY26; each executive director’s reported FY26 remuneration is ₹0.12 crore.

Repeated GST, TDS, EPF and ESIC delays include ESIC delays up to 605 days. The company attributes issues to filing/payment processes and says dues/returns were completed and a compliance officer appointed. Some leases were being regularized for stamping/registration. The unmodified statutory report does not erase these disclosed failures. The prospectus reports no company/promoter material litigation or company tax claim. An independent director’s ₹0.1558 crore tax demand remains under appeal; his response disputes reliance on undisclosed third-party material. That is not a company liability or a finding of issuer wrongdoing. The October price-movement response says the move was market-driven and required information disclosed; neither the query nor response establishes manipulation.

Promises versus delivery: rooftop scaling is evidenced through March; the IPP’s February commercial-operation claim has no FY26 revenue and needs billings/receipts; the August backlog is not converted cash; factory orders/approvals/commissioning within roughly six months of IPO remain unverified at cutoff. Monitoring should distinguish announced, ordered, installed, commissioned, revenue-generating and cash-returning milestones.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 EBITDA ₹14.5619 crore less depreciation ₹0.1119 crore gives EBIT ₹14.4500 crore; adding other income ₹0.1170 crore, subtracting finance cost ₹0.7816 crore and tax ₹3.5840 crore yields PAT ₹10.2014 crore. Most earnings are operating, but cash is the weaker link. CFO bridge starts at ₹14.7001 crore before WC, then inventory −₹6.9783 crore, receivables −₹11.2579 crore, advances −₹0.7809 crore, payables +₹1.3818 crore, other liabilities +₹1.7731 crore and tax −₹1.5401 crore, rounding to −₹2.7021 crore. FY26 cash capex ₹4.7633 crore gives FCF −₹7.4654 crore before financing interest. Three-year CFO/PAT is −0.0562×.

Receivables ₹11.3852 crore increased sharply from ₹0.2298 crore; closing DSO is 44.58 days versus 2.75 days in FY25. Related receivables account for about 20.10% of total. Inventory ₹12.7248 crore and short-term taxes ₹3.7629 crore require explicit attention. Aging primarily reflects recent expansion, so bad-debt loss is not assumed; collection proof matters more than management explanation. Contract assets/unbilled amounts are reported as absent in the receivable table, not synthesized.

Restated audited accounts are used consistently. FY24/FY25 PAT corrections are material, explicitly reconciled in the prospectus; FY26 statutory CFO −₹2.735125 crore becomes restated −₹2.7021 crore. FY25 noncash partner-capital transfer ₹2.3242 crore inflates two gross financing lines but not net cash. Historical cash/bank ₹0.8536 crore includes ₹0.3502 crore deposits outside cash equivalents; another ₹0.0522 crore deposit is noncurrent. Only ₹0.5034 crore is used as March opening cash, without claiming it is unrestricted today.

Operating invested capital is reconciled to financing sources after tax/deposit/nonoperating adjustments; FY25 residual ₹0.0002 crore is rounding. Normalized NOPAT uses 26% for comparison, not corrected reported PAT. FY26 average ROIC is 70.00% and ROCE 104.46%; small starting capital and mix changes prevent extrapolation. Current-share EPS ₹7.1660 differs from historical weighted EPS ₹10.86. The May 7:1 bonus changes presentation, not economic ownership; June placement and fresh IPO dilute. Term-debt current maturity is already included in short debt and is not counted twice. FY26 contingent liabilities and capital commitments are reported nil as of March, which does not extinguish later factory commitments. Prepaid March expenses are included once in operating capital; full IPO cash fees are conservatively deducted without assuming recovery of earlier costs. Operating leases are expensed under AS; no invented Ind AS lease balance is added.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹169.25, market capitalization is ₹240.9428 crore, historical current-share P/E 23.62× and sales 2.58×. Historical pre-IPO book or debt/cash multiples are stale after capital events and are labeled diagnostics, not current net debt or enterprise value. The model values EPC/trading, manufacturing and IPP operating EBITDA separately, then deducts remaining debt and retains operating cash. No extra value is assigned to operating land/plant already supporting enterprise value.

Bear/base/bull scenarios use rooftop counts and average ticket, ground-project growth, trading growth/spreads, separately conditional factory revenue and 1.2 MW IPP capacity with explicit CUF/tariff assumptions. Base EPC/trading margins are 18%/9%, factory ramp starts in FY28, and DSO/inventory are 50/65 days. Bear compresses margins to 11%/3.5%, increases DSO/inventory to 80/100 days and delays production. Bull requires sustained faster project growth, higher margin, quicker cash turns and successful new products; it is not guidance. Exit multiples differ by sector, not a single renewable premium.

The investor horizon ends on 20 October 2031. FY32 cash uses 203/366 of the fiscal year and terminal operating inputs blend FY31/FY32; post-terminal cash movements do not decide feasibility. Required reserve is conservatively retained using the FY32 annual revenue base. Signed cash minus reserves preserves deficits. Base and bull produce positive modeled cash, but current funding is not verified. Bear breaches the floor and needs a separate hypothetical ₹11.4658 crore gross equity raise at assumed ₹100 with 5% fees; share-count expansion 8.0542% is distinct from existing-holder dilution 7.4538%. This is a rescue counterfactual, not available finance.

Every ordinary return and entry-price field, including non-rescue conditional return, remains null. R and IAS therefore remain NS. Mechanical equity values are clearly non-investable diagnostics. No DCF is forced on unknown project returns; the annual cash model, sector terminal multiples, reverse earnings requirements, 12/15/18% hurdles, 9 cash/multiple sensitivities and 6 fully linked stresses are provided instead. At 15% the required five-year wealth multiple is 2.0114; at 12%/18% it is 1.7623/2.2878. No numerical entry range is supportable until the funding gate is resolved.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest contrary case is not that India stops buying solar equipment. It is that growth consumes cash faster than this young business earns it while management undertakes three manufacturing processes and an asset-owning generation activity. Collection slippage, more inventory, EPC margin compression and delayed equipment/customer acceptance can coincide. The linked stress treats these together, pays tax and demand debt, and does not assume lenders renew facilities or deposits are released. Bear minimum cash surplus is −₹10.8926 crore. The shortfall is not renamed debt or deleted from terminal valuation. Separate hypothetical equity funding dilutes existing owners and still leaves severe impairment risk.

A genuine buffer is the IPO and June capital raise plus profitable core EPC activity. The analysis does not declare insolvency, a covenant breach, manipulated price or an actual default. The thesis-break variables are sustained collection deterioration, total committed project spending beyond usable funds, recurring material compliance failures, or production spending without verified throughput/gross margin/receipts. A loss can arise even when revenue grows, through recapitalization, lower terminal multiples or failed returns on new capital. Management’s compliance and price-movement explanations are retained rather than treating unresolved questions as findings of wrongdoing.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A five-year 5×/10× share-price outcome requires about 37.97%/58.49% annualized appreciation. It is not established by historical small-base revenue growth, stated capacity or a renewable-market TAM. At unchanged shares, terminal P/E 15× and net margin 8%, 5× today’s market value requires approximately ₹1,003.93 crore revenue and 10× ₹2,007.86 crore. A lower 10× terminal P/E increases those needs to ₹1,505.89 crore and ₹3,011.78 crore. These are algebraic requirements, not forecasts; additional dilution raises required total earnings proportionately.

For a real outcome, EPC demand access, manufacturing qualification/utilization, supply-chain finance, cash conversion and minority per-share ownership must all survive scaling. Revenue, enterprise value, equity value and per-share stock return are different quantities. There is no independently verified accessible market-share bridge or funded reinvestment plan at that scale. Classification: Speculative / unsupported as a five-year multibagger thesis. Successful core growth may still create value without delivering these multiples.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Obtain the first post-IPO audited/reviewed utilization and cash bridge: begin with ₹31.32572 crore net IPO plus ₹7.0927992 crore June gross proceeds, reconcile actual costs, restricted balances and outstanding commitments. Warning: minimum required operating cash cannot be retained without new unspecified finance.
2. Track receivable cash collections against March ₹11.3852 crore and related ₹2.2881 crore. Warning: repeated DSO above the 50-day base assumption or material migration beyond 180 days without documented recovery.
3. Track inventory ₹12.7248 crore, slow-moving/obsolete solar products and cost-based turnover. Warning: persistent cash absorption around the 90–100-day inventory stress, not only sales growth.
4. Obtain split EPC/trading revenue, contribution margins and rooftop jobs; March baseline is 3,078 rooftop jobs and ₹54.5145 crore EPC. Warning: margin loss greater than 4 percentage points without lower capital needs.
5. Reconcile August orderbook ₹62.4419 crore into intake, execution, cancellations, invoicing and collections. Do not use gross new orders as cash.
6. Verify factory orders, landed/civil/all-in cost, all approvals, installation, trial yields, accepted commercial output and collections separately. Warning: spending rises while customer-qualified output remains absent.
7. Verify IPP actual MW definition, PPA tariff, meter generation/CUF, invoices and PGVCL receipts before assigning project returns. FY26 revenue baseline is zero.
8. Resolve demand-versus-2.5-year promoter debt, tax payments and term-debt service; no facility renewal or related funding is presumed.
9. Watch statutory filing/payment timeliness, RPT aging, pledge/lock-in changes and issuance.
10. Obtain official BSE 20/60-session tape once history exists, spread/depth and current restrictions; update the 1,200-share lot and position-specific capacity before any implementation conclusion.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. This is an early-stage EPC/trading expansion and manufacturing-optionality thesis, not a demonstrated compounder. It cannot meet the framework’s compounder requirements with MOAT 4, CASH 4 and CAP/BAL NS, nor can an incomplete BQS/GQS/IAS rank alongside complete issuer scores. High revenue growth is acknowledged, not treated as investment attractiveness. G3 and G4 remain unresolved for funding and execution-level tradability.

Conditional action is to resolve evidence before considering an allocation, not to buy at an invented target. Relevant changes are independently reconciled post-IPO resources and obligations, verified collections, attributable returns on new capital, operating production/IPP receipts and adequate tape/depth at the actual desired position. A lower price alone does not cure missing cash or liquidity evidence. Conversely, published credible funding and cash evidence could resolve a Hold without requiring access to private daily bank records. No ordinary IRR, entry range, personalized allocation or trading instruction is supplied.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence is the final September prospectus, FY26 statutory audit, predecessor-comparability notes, September shareholding and signed October price response. Exact source URLs, dates, SHA256 hashes and claim-level locators are supplied. Direct BSE admission/rolling pages returned 403; reproduced notice mirrors are explicitly secondary and cross-checked where possible. The 19 October quote is secondary and dated; a website landing page is not proof of current order execution. The official interoperable master verifies security reference fields, not daily BSE trading.

Historical units are INR crore except shares, per-share values and declared physical units. CFO/PAT and FCF are reported definitions; financing interest is separately retained. Normalized ROIC uses 26% NOPAT and average operating invested capital; historical incremental ROIC is diagnostic. Models use explicit analyst assumptions for tariff/CUF, margins, ramp, WC days, construction extras, tax and repayment timing. Their specificity is for reproducibility, not a claim those inputs are known.

Open questions are current usable funds and all-in committed project costs, borrowing terms, commissioning/approvals, manufacturing customer qualification and yields, IPP tariff/collections and 1 versus 1.2 MW description, orderbook conversion and exact liquidity restrictions/depth. The source-free private archives exclude original PDFs, raw HTML/OCR, images and shareholder identifiers. Reproduction can validate calculations and byte consistency from safe financial extracts; it cannot freshly authenticate the excluded original filings. No historical unknown is imputed as zero or a neutral score.

evidence.claim: Exact issuer is Infrax Renewable Limited, ISIN INE1YC401018, BSE SME 544919/INFRAX; 14,235,911 issued shares and 1,200-share lot.
evidence.locator: Prospectus cover, capital structure; September shareholding summary; exact-ISIN interoperable master.

evidence.claim: FY24/25/26 revenue ₹9.6524/30.4686/93.2149 crore and PAT ₹0.9576/2.8518/10.2014 crore. FY25 is the full predecessor-plus-company period, not the five-month company comparator.
evidence.locator: S1 printed pp 193–196 and 209–210; statutory S2 pp 13–15.
evidence.limitation: FY22/23 full comparable accounts and H1FY27 not established.

evidence.claim: FY26 EPC ₹54.5145 crore and trading ₹38.7003 crore; zero reported manufacturing or IPP revenue. Rooftop projects grew 664/1,964/3,078.
evidence.locator: Business pp 128–142; Annexure S printed p 224.
evidence.limitation: Segment revenue sum differs ₹0.0001 crore by rounding; segment profit is not reported.

evidence.claim: FY24–26 CFO ₹1.6724/0.2424/−2.7021 crore. Cumulative CFO/PAT is −0.05619236; cumulative FCF before financing interest is −₹5.7163 crore.
evidence.locator: Restated cash flow printed p 196; financial model.
evidence.limitation: Cash-flow statement presents finance interest in financing; interest-adjusted cash is separately calculated.

evidence.claim: FY26 inventory ₹12.7248 crore and receivables ₹11.3852 crore absorb growth cash. Restated CFO bridge includes −₹6.9783 crore inventory and −₹11.2579 crore receivables.
evidence.limitation: No later collection ledger or post-cutoff balances inferred.

evidence.claim: Restatement changes PAT from ₹1.6054/4.1250/10.2165 crore to ₹0.9576/2.8518/10.2014 crore for FY24/25/26; disclosed tax, benefits, depreciation and timing corrections. FY25 gross financing contains offsetting ₹2.3242 crore noncash partner-capital-to-loan transfer.
evidence.locator: Restatement printed pp 209–210; cash flow p 196 and partner-capital note.
evidence.limitation: Unmodified audit does not imply error-free accounts. Offset reclassification leaves net financing cash unchanged.

evidence.claim: FY26 debt ₹6.9867 crore; cash equivalents only ₹0.5034 crore, with ₹0.3502 crore longer-original-maturity current deposits and ₹0.0522 crore noncurrent deposits excluded from available cash.
evidence.locator: Printed pp 193,196,214–215,222 and financial indebtedness pp 239–241.
evidence.limitation: Deposits may be pledged; no release or post-IPO unrestricted balance assumed. Term debt includes current maturity and must not be added twice.

evidence.claim: Fresh IPO gross ₹33.80832 crore, allocated fees ₹2.4826 crore; net ₹31.32572 crore. OFS ₹7.07616 crore does not fund issuer. June placement ₹7.0927992 crore precedes listing. Objects reserve ₹12.2933 crore machinery, ₹17 crore WC and ₹2.0324 crore GCP.
evidence.locator: Cover, capital structure and objects printed pp 74–96.
evidence.limitation: Amounts are disclosed capital events, not verified unspent current cash. Existing July 2025 ₹4 crore equity already sits in FY26 figures.

evidence.claim: New manufacturing targets 3,000 tonnes/year solar recycling/silver extraction, 1,500 tonnes/year structures and 9.6 million frames/year. These are planned capacity, not output, sales or returns. Machinery quotes exclude taxes, civil works and installation items; approvals and commissioning remain to be evidenced.
evidence.locator: Objects pp 76–91 and business pp 123–145.
evidence.limitation: No verified post-IPO commissioning, equipment acceptance or attributable return evidence by cutoff.

evidence.claim: A 1.2 MW plant at Bhadla, Jasdan, Gujarat is described as operational from February 2026 under a 25-year PGVCL PPA, but FY26 IPP revenue is zero. Tariff/CUF and later receipts were not established.
evidence.locator: Business pp 133–134; policies pp 201–202; plant additions and commitment notes.
evidence.limitation: Commitment note refers to 1 MW; possible AC/DC distinction is unverified. Not the large Bhadla park in Rajasthan.

evidence.claim: Orderbook as of 20 August 2026: 3,100 projects and ₹62.4419 crore, against 1,756/₹35.8272 crore as of 31 May. June recognized amount ₹2.9744 crore is not current cash.
evidence.locator: Business printed p 129; earlier orderbook pp 130–132.
evidence.limitation: No complete intake/cancellation/conversion bridge, billed receivable schedule or project-level profitability.

evidence.claim: Gujarat accounts for 97.41% of FY26 revenue. Top customer 13.61%, top five 39.21%, top ten 47.02%; top supplier 21.09% and top ten 65.86%. Dealer network 2,830, with installation mainly through third parties and four technical staff of 52 total staff.
evidence.locator: Risk pp 23–37; business pp 128–146.
evidence.limitation: Dealer count is distribution reach, not evidence of captive customers or a moat.

evidence.claim: Infrax Solar LLP FY26 related sales ₹4.0143 crore, purchases ₹3.7390 crore and receivable ₹2.2881 crore. ₹0.25 crore advances to relatives were repaid; directors each received ₹0.12 crore FY26 remuneration.
evidence.locator: Related-party annexure printed pp 230–232.
evidence.limitation: Amounts exclude cumulative multi-year sums. No substantiated diversion inferred from ordinary related trade alone.

evidence.claim: Repeated GST/TDS/EPF/ESIC delays are disclosed. FY25 ESIC delays extend to 605 days; company says returns and dues were completed, and a compliance officer appointed. Some leases need stamping/registration regularization.
evidence.locator: Risk printed pp 32–33 and statutory audit CARO.
evidence.limitation: Audit reports no material extended statutory arrears; disclosed lateness is preserved with management response, not treated as fraud.

evidence.claim: September promoter ownership 7,079,600 shares (49.73%); public 7,156,311 (50.27%). Promoter pledge zero; 10,304,711 total shares locked, leaving arithmetic unlocked 3,931,200, not order-book liquidity.
evidence.locator: Shareholding summary and lock-in aggregate columns.
evidence.limitation: No holder-level identifying information retained in analytical artifacts.

evidence.claim: ₹169.25 dated 19 October 2026 secondary close is cross-checked. One-day volume 96,000 shares and traded value ₹170.88 lakh are not a complete 20/60-session series.
evidence.locator: Quote timestamp and historical date/value fields.
evidence.limitation: Official BSE daily tape and executable spread/depth were not retrieved.

evidence.claim: Company responded on 19 October that price movement is market-driven, management has no knowledge of reasons, and required disclosures have been/will be made.
evidence.locator: Signed price-movement response, one page.
evidence.limitation: Exchange query and issuer response do not by themselves establish price manipulation.

evidence.claim: A 2.5-year promoter-loan description conflicts with the on-demand note. Conservative model pays the ₹1.586 crore in FY27; no actual default is asserted.
evidence.locator: Annexure B(B), printed p 215; financial indebtedness p 240.
evidence.limitation: Loan timing needs clarification before establishing current funding.

evidence.claim: Separate operating models link rooftop project volumes/tickets, ground EPC, trading margins, proposed manufacturing ramp and IPP CUF/tariff to WC, capex, tax, debt and cash.
evidence.locator: model.py/model.json and source assumptions.
evidence.limitation: These are analytical scenarios, not guidance, current cash evidence or project approval.

evidence.claim: Historical peers in the prospectus represent different economics: ACME Solar is asset-owning IPP; Alpex is module manufacturing; Solarium is EPC. A single renewable P/E comparison is misleading.
evidence.locator: Basis for issue price, printed pp 102–109.
evidence.limitation: Issuer-reproduced peer data not independently reconciled; no current peer-pricing recommendation.

evidence.claim: Company/promoter material litigation and company tax claims are reported nil; an independent director has disputed direct-tax demand ₹0.1558 crore, pending appeal with a response disputing third-party evidence. FY26 contingent liabilities and capital commitments are reported nil at March date, not for new post-IPO projects.
evidence.locator: Litigation printed pp 264–267; Annexure AE printed p 233.
evidence.limitation: No adverse finding against the issuer inferred; post-IPO obligations must be separately established.

reconciliations: FY25 statutory company comparator covers 1 November 2024 to 31 March 2025, unlike the full-year restated predecessor-plus-company period. Do not mix these.
The prospectus restates taxes, employee benefits, depreciation and timing errors. FY26 PAT 10.2165 becomes 10.2014; FY25 4.1250 becomes 2.8518; FY24 1.6054 becomes 0.9576.

FY25 financing gross lines include noncash transfer of 2.3242 from partner capital to director/shareholder debt. Net reported financing cash flow is unchanged when both offsetting gross entries are removed.
The proposal WC table uses statutory values, some different from restated balances, and deducts tax provisions. It is not the analytical operating NWC definition.

FY26 balance-sheet cash/bank 0.8536 includes 0.3502 in longer-original-maturity deposits; cash-flow cash equivalents are only 0.5034. Another 0.0522 deposit is noncurrent. No automatic release assumed.
The prospectus records promoter loans as on-demand in Annexure B(B) but 2.5 years in Financial Indebtedness. Use demand repayment in the stress model until clarified.

valuation_cross_checks.stale_balance_EV_proxy_note: Not current EV; omits post-March capital/spending. No misuse of deposits or IPO money as free cash.
valuation_cross_checks.dcf_reason: Undisclosed project tariff/returns and fresh manufacturing ramp would create false precision; explicit sector cash/funding and terminal multiple model used instead.

model_limitations: Annual operating forecasts are assumptions, not management guidance.
FY27 pre-entry roll-forward is estimated and never represented as actual cash.
Manufacturing starts as zero historical revenue. Its forecast contribution is explicitly conditional on licences, equipment, production yields and customer qualification.
No undisclosed facilities or tax refunds finance a gap.
Contracted 25-year PPA is not 25 years of guaranteed equity return; tariff/CUF are assumptions.
All ordinary returns and entry prices remain null; rescue figures are separate counterfactual diagnostics.

market.status: Dated secondary close and one-day trading diagnostic; not official tape

ownership.status: 30 September aggregate filing; unlocked does not equal readily purchasable float

tape_status.reason: Listed fewer than 60 trading sessions by cutoff. Complete BSE daily tape not retrieved; absent NSE rows are missing, not zero.

liquidity.conclusion: One lot costs ₹203,100. At 2%/5%/10% of the quoted single day value, whole-lot capacities are 1/4/8 lots. That is a single-day arithmetic diagnostic, not promised execution or a 60-session exit forecast. No verified 60-session tape, order-book depth, queues or current restrictions; do not score L from one day or impute missing observations as zero.
